version.changelog:
- 强化了 MCP 服务的调用规范：明确要求调用带参数的 MCP 工具时必须使用完整结构化 JSON，并严禁 mcporter 调用遗漏 --args 参数。
- 明确全局规则，补充了 MCP 相关的错误场景与参数传递说明。
- 其他内容无实质变更，仅文档细节微调。

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: yuketang-mcp
Version: 1.0.326681

The skill bundle provides a legitimate integration for 'Rain Classroom' (Yuketang), a Chinese educational platform. The setup scripts (setup.sh, setup.js) and instructions (SKILL.md) are focused on configuring an MCP server to query classroom data, student warnings, and teaching statistics. While the setup script includes a telemetry call (claw_report) to report installation duration to the service provider's endpoint (xuetangx.com), this behavior is transparent and aligned with the stated purpose of the tool. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's behavior largely matches its education/query purpose, but there are inconsistencies and privacy/operational risks (it requires a secret that the registry metadata omits, the included setup scripts register a client and silently report installation telemetry, and they pass the secret on the command line).

dimensions.detail: The skill is for querying Yuketang (雨课堂) via an MCP server and the package.json declares an mcp_url and env-based auth (YUKETANG_SECRET), which is coherent with the described functionality. However the registry metadata at the top incorrectly lists no required environment variables while SKILL.md, package.json, and the setup scripts require YUKETANG_SECRET — an inconsistency that should have been declared.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs users to set YUKETANG_SECRET and run setup.sh / setup.js which register an MCP service and verify it. The instructions also require the agent to assist users in updating environment variables when users provide secrets. The setup scripts perform remote calls via mcporter (including a silent 'install' report) and rely on npx mcporter to configure and call the remote MCP server; this goes beyond mere local guidance and results in network activity to the declared mcp_url.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no arbitrary download from unknown hosts; installation relies on included setup.sh/setup.js which call npx mcporter. Using npx is a common pattern but causes transient downloads/execution from npm at runtime. The scripts do not extract archives from arbitrary URLs and do not write unknown binaries, but they will alter MCP client configuration (project scope) when successful.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill legitimately needs a service secret (YUKETANG_SECRET) to authenticate to the MCP endpoint, but the top-level metadata omitted this requirement. The setup scripts pass the secret as a CLI argument to npx mcporter (Authorization=Bearer <secret>), which can expose the secret via process arguments or shell history on some systems. The scripts also use the secret to register and then send a silent telemetry call — small in content but still a networked use of the secret.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false (normal). The setup scripts will register an MCP server in the user's project-scoped MCP config (expected for this kind of skill). There is no code that attempts to modify other skills or system-wide agent settings beyond adding the MCP server config. The silent telemetry call during setup increases the footprint briefly by making a network call.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is intended to talk to a Yuketang MCP server and needs your YUKETANG_SECRET. Before installing: (1) confirm the secret URL (https://www.yuketang.cn/ai-workspace/open-claw-skill) is legitimate and that you trust the skill source (source/homepage are unknown here); (2) inspect setup.sh and setup.js yourself — they will call 'npx mcporter config add' and may pass your secret as a command-line argument, which can be visible to other processes or in shell history; (3) the installer makes a silent 'install' telemetry call to the MCP server — expect network traffic to the mcp_url in package.json; (4) if you are concerned, manually add the MCP config using a placeholder Authorization value (the scripts print a manual config template), or run the setup in an isolated environment; and (5) ask the skill author or maintainer to correct the registry metadata to declare YUKETANG_SECRET explicitly. If you proceed, minimize risk by using a limited-scope secret, running installation in a safe environment, and monitoring network/process activity.
